author: reek
body: The reset arm is the one that earns its place. A PHY reset returns the paged registers to their defaults, so slow mode set BEFORE the reset is gone by the time any read needs it; the driver sets it after, and this reads a register that is only reachable if that ordering held.

author: reek
body: Before any bring-up the mode is at its reset default, so an ordinary register read is refused and comes back as the error sentinel.

author: reek
body: The page register answers while ordinary reads do not. That separates a gated bus from a dead one: if this also failed, the arm would be indistinguishable from -e1000-no-phy and would prove nothing about pages.

author: reek
body: A page nothing is modelled on must answer error rather than zero, the same distinction e1000-phy-read-at draws for an unanswered address.

author: reek
body: After a full bring-up the ordinary read that failed above succeeds, and it succeeds only if slow mode was set on the far side of the PHY reset.
